reference: He had been training for hours before the light was finally right.
sk: Trénoval hodiny, kým bolo svetlo konečne správne.
cz: Trénoval hodiny, než bylo světlo konečně správné.
acceptable: He had been {training|practising|practicing} for {hours|several hours|many hours} before the {light|lighting} {was finally right|finally was right|was right at last}.
He had been {training|practising|practicing} for {hours|several hours|many hours} until the {light|lighting} was finally right.
For hours he had been {training|practising|practicing} before the {light|lighting} was finally right.

mistakes.text: He was training for hours {before|until} the light was finally right.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Dej trval až do iného minulého deja, preto Past Perfect Continuous: „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Děj trval až do jiného minulého děje, proto Past Perfect Continuous: „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_en: The training lasted up to another past event, so use the Past Perfect Continuous: “had been training”.

mistakes.text: He trained for hours {before|until} the light was finally right.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Na trvanie pred iným minulým dejom sa lepšie hodí Past Perfect Continuous: „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Na trvání před jiným minulým dějem se lépe hodí Past Perfect Continuous: „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_en: To stress duration before another past event, the Past Perfect Continuous “had been training” fits better.

mistakes.text: He had trained for hours {before|until} the light was finally right.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Dôraz je na trvaní („for hours“), preto je lepší Past Perfect Continuous: „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Důraz je na trvání („for hours“), proto je lepší Past Perfect Continuous: „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_en: The focus is on duration (“for hours”), so the Past Perfect Continuous “had been training” is better.

mistakes.text: He had been training since hours {before|until} the light was finally right.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Pri dĺžke trvania patrí „for“, nie „since“: „for hours“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: U délky trvání patří „for“, ne „since“: „for hours“.
mistakes.feedback_en: Use “for” with a length of time, not “since”: “for hours”.

mistakes.text: He has been training for hours {before|until} the light was finally right.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Všetko sa stalo v minulosti, preto nie „has been“, ale „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Všechno se stalo v minulosti, proto ne „has been“, ale „had been training“.
mistakes.feedback_en: Everything happened in the past, so not “has been” but “had been training”.
